intent_doc_match.section: fix(walkthrough): General settings fields lived in a separate form from the Save button, so saving never submitted them
intent_doc_match.quote: The General section was wrapped in its own <form action=save_settings> with no submit button, while the 'Save Settings' button sat in a separate <form action=save_settings> holding only the instance fields; clicking Save submitted only the instances form, so every General field (skip_unreleased, log_level, counts, etc.) was absent from the POST and reset to its form-default on each save.

findings.problem: This working-tree diff exactly undoes HEAD commit 542d5dd. It wraps the General section in its own <form action=save_settings> again (line 18 to 90). That form has no submit button. The diff also removes id="settings-form" from the instances form and drops every form="settings-form" attribute. Two templates use this pattern to avoid illegal nested forms: the General fields, and the add-instance inputs at lines 230-232 with form="add-{{ app_name }}", whose target forms are defined at line 250. When the user clicks 'Save Settings' (line 241, inside the instances form at line 134), only instance fields are posted. save_settings (triggarr/web/routes.py:531-539) then sees no General fields and falls back to the defaults from safe_int/safe_log_level. skip_unreleased is set from form.get("skip_unreleased") == "on", so it becomes False on every save.

findings.fix_hint: Discard the working-tree change (git checkout triggarr/templates/settings.html). This restores id="settings-form" on the instances form and form="settings-form" on every General control.
findings.why_it_matters: Each click of Save silently resets all General settings (log level, limits, timeouts, skip_unreleased) to their defaults. The walkthrough had already caught and fixed this bug. The regression test test_general_fields_submit_with_the_save_settings_form (tests/test_web.py:832) checks for 'id="settings-form"', so it will fail.

members.title: General settings form has no submit button again, so General fields can't be saved
members.problem: This diff reverses fix 542d5dd. It wraps the General section in its own <form action=save_settings> (lines 18-90), and that form has no submit button. The only 'Save Settings' button (lines 240-245) is in a separate <form> (line 134), and that form only holds the instance fields. The diff also removes form="settings-form" from every General control and the id="settings-form" from the instances form. With no submit button, implicit submission does not fire, because the General form has several fields that block it. So the General form can never be submitted from the UI.
members.why_it_matters: Users can't change log level, the hard max, history rows, the timeout, page size, the tracking window, max failures or skip_unreleased from the UI.
members.fix_hint: restore id="settings-form" on the instances form and form="settings-form" on each General control (revert this diff)

members.title: Diff reverts the committed fix for General settings fields never saving, discarding the documented form-association convention
members.problem: Global CLAUDE.md: 'before introducing a new pattern, check how the same problem is solved elsewhere in the repo and follow that.' This diff removes the form="settings-form" attribute from every General-section control and the id="settings-form" on the instances <form>, replacing the documented convention with a standalone <form> for General that has no submit button. Project CLAUDE.md also requires (Deep Code Review Convention #2) 'All tests pass (pytest tests/ -x)' — this diff fails that check outright.
members.why_it_matters: This is byte-for-byte the inverse of commit 542d5dd, which fixed exactly this regression and added tests/test_web.py::test_general_fields_submit_with_the_save_settings_form as a guard. Ran that test: it fails with 'instances form must declare id=settings-form'. Shipping this means every General setting silently resets to its form-default on every 'Save Settings' click.
members.fix_hint: Revert to the pattern this diff removes: give the instances <form> back id="settings-form" and restore form="settings-form" on every General-section control, per commit 542d5dd.

members.title: Diff reverts fix 542d5dd: General settings sit in their own form with no submit button, so every Save Settings click resets them to handler defaults
members.problem: This diff is an exact inverse of commit 542d5dd. After the change, the General controls live in <form action=save_settings> at settings.html:18-90, and that form has no submit button. The only submit buttons in the file are the Security form's Save (line 109) and 'Save Settings' (line 241), which is inside the second, id-less save_settings form (lines 134-246) that holds only the instance fields. When a user clicks Save Settings, the POST has no General fields. save_settings (triggarr/web/routes.py:530-539) then rebuilds the whole general block from form.get(...) with fallbacks and writes it to the TOML: log_level goes to the safe_log_level default, hard_max_per_cycle to 0, max_history_rows to 1000, request_timeout to 30, page_size to 50, tracking_window_minutes to 60, max_consecutive_failures to 5, and skip_unreleased to False. Pressing Enter inside the General form does not submit it either. Any instance edit also silently overwrites the operator's General config.
members.why_it_matters: This is a regression to a bug a walkthrough already found and fixed. Each UI save quietly changes persisted config: skip_unreleased flips to False, so searches start running for unreleased items, and hard caps and timeouts fall back to defaults.
members.fix_hint: Drop this working-tree change: restore the form="settings-form" attributes, the <div> wrapper and id="settings-form" on the instances form, as in HEAD 542d5dd.

members.title: Restore General fields' association with the Save Settings form
members.problem: The General controls now belong to a separate form with no submit button. Clicking Save Settings submits only the instance form, omitting every General value. In triggarr/web/routes.py:531-539, save_settings replaces missing values with defaults and persists them: for example, a configured hard_max_per_cycle=10 becomes 0 (unlimited), and checked skip_unreleased becomes false. General edits are discarded, and even saving an unrelated instance change overwrites existing General settings. The existing test_general_fields_submit_with_the_save_settings_form explicitly guards this regression.
members.why_it_matters: General edits are discarded, and even saving an unrelated instance change overwrites existing General settings.
members.fix_hint: Restore id="settings-form" on the instance form and form="settings-form" on every General control, keeping Security separate. Run the existing form-association regression test.

findings.title: Each Save Settings click resets every General setting to its default
findings.problem: Clicking Save submits only the instances form, so no General field is in the POST. save_settings (triggarr/web/routes.py:529-540) builds 'general' straight from form.get(...) and does not fall back to the current settings. safe_int then returns the hardcoded defaults: hard_max 0, history 1000, timeout 30, page_size 50, window 60, failures 5. safe_log_level(None) returns 'info', and skip_unreleased becomes False because form.get returns None, which is != 'on'. The result passes validation and is written to config, so the user's General configuration is silently overwritten on every save. This is the exact regression described in commit 542d5dd.
findings.fix_hint: restore the form="settings-form" association so General fields submit with the Save button
findings.why_it_matters: Silent loss of configuration. For example, skip_unreleased turns off and the log level resets every time the user saves instance settings.

members.title: Removing id="settings-form" breaks the regression test test_general_fields_submit_with_the_save_settings_form
members.problem: tests/test_web.py:853 asserts 'id="settings-form"' in text, and the lines after it require every General control to reference that form. The diff removes the id from the instances form and removes form="settings-form" from all eight General controls, so this test will fail. CI and the CLAUDE.md pre-push gate (pytest tests/ -x) will block the change.
members.why_it_matters: The test suite goes red and the specific guard for the walkthrough bug is defeated.
members.fix_hint: Revert the template change. If the layout must change, keep every General control associated with the form that holds the Save Settings button.
